s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin laxity with flexural papules and calcification of elastic fibers
salient_findings: Progressive skin laxity since childhood
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Severe skin sagging with loss of elasticity
Thick and leathery skinfolds
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
key_facts: 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas since early childhood
Severe skin sagging occurred on the abdomen with loss of elasticity
Skin symptoms spread extensively with developmental growth
No extracutaneous involvement
Born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
Younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds)
Normal echocardiographic examination results
Normal fundoscopic examination results
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis on skin biopsy
Compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
